full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: In this Rule Nisi the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the ex parte decree dated 23-9-2003 (decree signed on 30-9-2003) and the provision of section 19(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the order dated 19-6-2004 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners and proceeding of the said Artha Rin Execution No. 4 of 2003 pending in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The material fact, in short, for disposal of this Rule is that the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No. 3 of 2002 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah impleading the petitioners for realisation of Taka 10,63,867. The defendants duly appeared in the suit and filed joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. 

 4. Against the said ex parte judgment and decree dated 23-9-2003 the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2003 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Jhenaidah for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 23-9-2003. 

 5. The learned Judge of the Adalat upon hearing the parties disallowed the said Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2003 on the ground that the petitioners did not deposit 10% of the decretal amount as per provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter called the Ain, 2003). 

 6. In usual course the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank, put the decree into execution by filing the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 in order to realise the decretal amount including interest by selling the petitioners' mortgaged property. 

 7. During pendency of the execution case the decree-holder-Bank filed an application under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter called the AM, 2003) praying for passing an order of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The Adalat, on consideration of the materials on record, issued warrant of arrest by his order dated 19-6-2004. 

 9. Mr Abdul Jalil, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, in the course of argument after placing the writ petition along with Annexure submits that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, under misconception of law and facts, most illegally and mechanically after rejecting the application for adjournment filed by the defendant-petitioners took up the case for ex parte hearing and passed the impugned ex parte judgment and decree dated 23-9-2003 which is not tenable in law. He next submits that the provision of section 19(3) of the Ain, 2003 depositing 10% of the decretal amount while filing a petition for setting-aside ex parte decree is arbitrary and violative of the provisions of the Constitution and, as such, the same is liable to be struck down. 

 11. Lastly, Mr Abdul Jalil contends that in view of the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003, an Execution Case has to be disposed of within a period of 90 days or at least within the next sixty days but the present Execution Case has been filed on 15-12-2003 in which 90+60= 150 days has already been expired and therefore, the continuation of the proceeding of the Execution Case is clear violation of the Mandatory Provision of section 37 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and hence at any rate the impugned proceeding of the execution case is liable to be declared illegal and void. 

 12. On the other hand, Mrs Khursheed Jahan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank by filing affidavit-in-opposition supports the impugned judgment and decree as well as the proceeding of the Execution Case, which were, according to her, just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate in the course of argument after placing the affidavit-in-opposition, straight forward submits that the instant writ petition was filed challenging judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which is misconceived and not maintainable in law, inasmuch as by now it has been well settled that no writ petition lies against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat since there is a forum/specific provision in the Ain for seeking remedy against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Mrs Khursheed Jahan in support of her submissions relied on the cases reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD) 6 & 59 DLR (AD) 6. 

 15. In the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, where it has been decided as follows: 

 16. In the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, where the principle has been laid down in the following terms: 

 17. In the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6, it has been decided: 

 "In view of the decisions quoted above we are led to irresistible conclusion that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant by not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain the writ petition." 

 18. For a reading of the above quoted uniform decisions of our Apex Court, we find a clear view of the law as it stands today that an application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not lie against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat since there being specific provision in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent Bank that the instant writ petition is misconceived and not maintainable. 

 19. In the case of Anisur Rahman @ KM Ziaul Haque vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 12 BLC 22, where it has been observed that the provisions of section 19 of the Ain, 2003 giving right to the borrowers to redress against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, whether ex parte or contested, it cannot be said that such defaulting borrowers have lost their fundamental right of protection of law or to be treated in accordance with law as enshrined in Article 31 of the Constitution. 

 21. To meet the contention of Mr Abdul Jalil, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, that the continuation of the proceeding of the execution case beyond 90+60=150 days is clear violation of the mandatory provision of section 37 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, we have examined the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 as best as we could do. Section 37 of the Ain, 2003 provides a time-frame for disposal of the execution case, although the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 does not provide for the consequence if the proceeding of the execution case runs beyond 150 days. 

 22. Thus, it is apparent that the requirement of time-frame for disposal of an execution case as laid down in section 37 of the Ain, 2003, is merely directory and not mandatory. So, it cannot be said that if the execution case is not disposed of within 90+60=150 days it will be automatically stopped or dismissed. This view of ours finds support in the case of Khurshed Alam (Md) vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat-1 reported in 12 BLC 592. 

 32. The Artha Rin Adalat, Jhenaidah is directed to proceed with the Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 expeditiously.
